description: This dataset is a de-duplicated, located list of cattle auction markets in the United States, compiled from four directories including the USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service list of facilities approved for interstate livestock handling. The Dataverse page says auction markets are hubs in the cattle transport network where animals from separate farms meet, so they matter for disease spread (as in the 2001 foot-and-mouth epidemic in the UK), and that no complete US list existed before. Version 3.1 (published 2014, updated 7 August 2015) by Ian Carroll and Shweta Bansal has a market table of about 320 KB, a market-to-county table and a readme, downloadable and free under CC0 1.0, with national coverage. Caveats: the list reflects directories around 2014 and markets open and close. For simulation it gives the hub nodes of livestock movement networks for agent-based outbreak models, and sites whose closure during a disease or transport disruption would stall cattle supply. Related catalogue records include FLAPS simulated livestock farms and the global livestock distribution 1 km data.
